themes.theme: RNG seed is the only numeric core option that is silently coerced (via >>> 0) instead of validated, so invalid/out-of-range/non-integer seeds silently alias onto other seeds at the two public entry points and their internal buddy-graph callers, unlike every other numeric option (k, mind, minDist, polishIters, priorWeight) which throw or fall back explicitly.
findingSummaries: `RNG` accepts any number as a seed and coerces it with `>>> 0`, so non-integer, negative and >= 2**32 seeds silently alias onto other seeds — the only numeric option in the core that is not validated, while k, mind, minDist, polishIters and priorWeight all throw or fall back explicitly for exactly this reason.
themes.remediation: Remove the silent `>>> 0` coercion path: validate seed once at the two public entry points (polish, polishConstrained) using the same throw-shaped check already used for priorWeight/polishIters, and delete the separate ad hoc normalization currently duplicated in buildBuddyGraph/buildConstrainedBuddyGraph so there is a single seed-acceptance path instead of two.

themes.theme: repairDegrees' internal work-budget counter estimates per-sweep cost from the target degree k rather than measuring the graph's actual edge count, so a hostile/skewed graph shape (edges >> n*k/2) undercharges the counter without bound and the budget never binds — the same failure the counter was supposedly introduced to close, and repairDegrees is also the one generator missing the size cap every other path in the module carries.
findingSummaries: `repairDegrees`'s runtime work counter charges each `bfsDistances` sweep `sweepCost = g.n + g.n * k` — a cost model derived from the TARGET degree k, not the sweep's actual cost `g.n + 2*g.numEdges()`. For any caller-supplied graph whose real edge count exceeds `n*k/2`, the counter undercharges without bound, so the budget never binds and the call runs to completion in tens of minutes. `repairDegrees` is also the only generator with no size cap at all, against the module doctrine that every path needs both a size cap and a work cap; polish/polishConstrained were given checkPolishSize computed from the ACTUAL m for exactly this reason.
themes.remediation: Delete the k-derived cost estimate and charge each sweep its real, already-available cost (`g.n + 2 * g.numEdges()`, recomputed inside the while(changed) loop); this alone removes the separate size-cap gap too, since refusing up front when that same real-cost expression exceeds a fixed share of MAX_REPAIR_WORK reuses the corrected formula rather than adding a new one.

gating.theme: a numeric option is silently coerced instead of validated, so distinct settings collapse onto one output and the caller cannot tell
gating.summary: `RNG` accepts any number as a seed and coerces it with `>>> 0`, so non-integer, negative and >= 2**32 seeds silently alias onto other seeds — the only numeric option in the core that is not validated, while k, mind, minDist, polishIters and priorWeight all throw or fall back explicitly for exactly this reason.
gating.failure: `polish(ring(16), {seed: 0})`, `{seed: 2**32}`, `{seed: 12884901888}`, `{seed: NaN}`, `{seed: 0.9}` and `{seed: -0}` all return byte-identical edge lists; likewise `buildBuddyGraph(24, 4, {seed: 12345})` is byte-identical to `{seed: 12345.6}`, `{seed: 12345 + 2**32}` and `{seed: -4294954951}`. A caller asking for a different arrangement with any of those values gets the same graph back with no error and no signal. Reproduced with /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/p12.mjs.
gating.remediation: Validate the seed at the two public entry points that take it (`polish`, `polishConstrained`), in the same shape as the adjacent `priorWeight` / `polishIters` checks: throw `seed ${s} must be an integer in [0, 4294967296)` for anything else, or normalise it once in one place and document the domain on `PolishOptions.seed` / `PolishConstrainedOptions.seed`. Close the theme, not the case: the sibling is `buildBuddyGraph` / `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph`, which forward `options.seed` unchecked and whose documented contract is to refuse rather than throw — they should normalise the way they already do for a bad `priorWeight`.
gating.invariant: For every seed value `s` that `polish`/`polishConstrained` accept without throwing, `Number.isInteger(s) && s >= 0 && s < 2**32`; equivalently, no two distinct accepted seed values produce the same RNG stream (`new RNG(s1)` and `new RNG(s2)` with `s1 !== s2` differ within their first output).

gating.theme: a generation budget that models per-unit cost from the requested degree instead of measuring the graph it was handed lets a hostile graph shape run for minutes past the ceiling the budget advertises
gating.summary: `repairDegrees`'s runtime work counter charges each `bfsDistances` sweep `sweepCost = g.n + g.n * k` — a cost model derived from the TARGET degree k, not the sweep's actual cost `g.n + 2*g.numEdges()`. For any caller-supplied graph whose real edge count exceeds `n*k/2` (i.e. whenever k is smaller than the graph's actual degrees), the counter undercharges without bound, so the budget never binds and the call runs to completion in tens of minutes. This is the same class of defect the counter was introduced to close (a predicted model that tracked the calibration shapes and admitted a 239 s call) — the counter fixed the PASS-count model but kept a modelled unit cost, so the comment's claim that "a counter cannot be wrong about the shape" and `budgets.ts`'s calibration note that "every refusal is reached in under 10 s" are both false. `repairDegrees` is also the only generator with no size cap at all, against the module doctrine (budgets.ts header) that every path needs both a size cap and a work cap; `polish`/`polishConstrained` were given `checkPolishSize` computed from the ACTUAL m for exactly this reason.
gating.failure: Build g = clique on 2000 vertices plus 4000 degree-1 leaves (two per clique vertex): n=6000, m=2,003,000. Call `repairDegrees(g, 2)` (exported from the package index). Measured: returns normally after 32.8 s. Instrumented copy of the same function reports final `work` = 93,001,681 against MAX_REPAIR_WORK = 1,000,000,000 (9.3% of budget) while performing 8.03e9 real adjacency-traversal steps across 2000 sweeps — an 86x undercharge, and no refusal is ever raised. The same construction at n=12000, m=8,006,000 ran for over 10 minutes. Contrast the documented calibration, which claims every refusal lands under 10 s. Harnesses: /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/repair.mjs and /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/instrumented.mjs.
gating.remediation: Charge each sweep its real cost rather than a k-derived estimate: compute the edge total once per pass (`const sweepCost = g.n + 2 * g.numEdges()`, refreshed inside the `while (changed)` loop since repair adds edges) instead of `g.n + g.n * k`. Additionally give `repairDegrees` the size cap the doctrine requires — the analogue of `checkPolishSize`: refuse up front when a single sweep `g.n + 2*g.numEdges()` already exceeds a fixed share of MAX_REPAIR_WORK, so the pre-loop shape is refused rather than discovered after the first multi-second sweep. Ratchet the invariant below as a property test over generated graphs whose m is decoupled from n*k (cliques-with-leaves, dense cores with sparse fringes), asserting charged >= actual rather than asserting a wall-clock time.
gating.invariant: For every Graph g and every integer k >= 0, the work charged by `repairDegrees` for each `bfsDistances` sweep is >= that sweep's actual traversal cost `g.n + 2 * g.numEdges()`; equivalently, total charged work is an upper bound on total adjacency-traversal steps performed, for ALL graphs — not only those whose edge count happens to be ~n*k/2.
